deadline.value: Apply by January 15, 2027 for full financial aid consideration for Fall admission (applications accepted until March 15).
deadline.quote: Graduate program application deadlines | Fall start | January 15 to receive full consideration for Financial Aid. Applications will continue to be accepted until March 15.

gre_general.value: GRE General Test scores are not required but may be submitted if available.
gre_general.quote: GRE tests are not required, however GRE scores can be submitted with the application, if available.

gre_subject.value: The Physics GRE Subject Test is not required but is strongly encouraged.
gre_subject.quote: The subject test in physics is not required but is strongly encouraged.

supervisor.value: The Department of Physics does not state whether applicants must contact or secure a faculty advisor prior to admission.

also.quote: As a graduate student, you will work closely with an advisor and an advisory committee to develop your plan of study. You will complete a substantial research project under the supervision of your faculty advisor.

funding.value: The department awards up to two physics fellowships per year along with teaching assistantships and other graduate support; apply by January 15 for full financial aid consideration.
funding.quote: Each year the department will allocate up to two physics fellowships in current areas of research for exceptional candidates. | From teaching assistantships to travel fellowships, there are a number of ways you can find help funding your education.

entry_route.value: Applicants may enter with an undergraduate degree in physics or a related science/engineering field; the Ph.D. requires 90 credit hours.
entry_route.quote: To enroll in a physics graduate program, you should have a background in the usual undergraduate courses in physics, math, and other sciences. If your undergraduate degree is from a related field of study in pure and applied sciences and engineering, you may be accepted on a probationary basis until you complete any necessary undergraduate physics courses.
